correctness.rationale: The inner-function Wold layer model matches the source: d-coordinate equal-sum homogeneous vectors give B_d e_l=sqrt((l+1)/(l+d))e_(l+1), and each transverse basis vector yields a reducing copy of K_i tensor l2; finite multiplicity D_i is essential. Defect equations A*T=TA*=0, I-A*A=T*T and I-AA*=TT* reduce C_i to R_l=a_l|1><1|-b_l|eta_i/z><eta_i/z| with a_l=(d-1)/(l+d-1), b_l=(d-1)/(l+d). For overlap alpha=|eta_i'(0)|<1, rank-two characteristic trace a_l-b_l and determinant -a_lb_l(1-alpha²) yield signed eigenvalues with l*r_(l,+) and l*|r_(l,-)| tending to (d-1)beta. D_i copies of two branches imply tN(t)->2D_i(d-1)beta and monotone inversion gives n mu_n and logarithmic-mean limits. If alpha=1, Schwarz equality forces eta_i=phase*z, P=Q, all blocks are rank-one positive a_l-b_l and telescope to D_i exactly. Independently recalculated rational block discriminants/endpoint identities; finite spectra in verify_endpoint.py are diagnostics only. The model is genuine operator decomposition, not a Hilbert-Schmidt-log extrapolation.
residual_risks: Assumes finite transverse D_i; an infinite transverse tensor multiplicity invalidates compactness and rearrangement.

value.rationale: A sharp Schatten-1 boundary and noncommutative residue for a concrete class of compressed multipliers fills a natural endpoint gap left by Hilbert-Schmidt and p>1 estimates.
